title: Hosted API: Consumption Eligibility & Routing Playbook for Enterprise Multi-Action Requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Create a deterministic, SLA-aware playbook that governs which inbound enterprise feature requests for the Hosted API (multi-action chat + streaming + tool/function calls + structured outputs) are eligible for self-serve vs. require sales/solutions escalation, and how requests are routed to product, eng, or platform tracks.

Scope: Non-bug feature requests that change request handling, routing, or contract surface for hosted API customers. Includes: new streaming controls, multi-tool orchestration contracts, structured output schema obligations, tenant isolation knobs, and enterprise SLAs tied to throughput/latency/retention. Excludes infra-only reliability incidents, pricing negotiations, and purely backend infra capacity purchases (Dedicated/Private intake covers those).

Goals:
- Reduce intake decision time from >5 business days to 24–48 hours for high-priority enterprise signals.
- Provide clear eligibility checks (security, data residency, SLO needs, customer revenue tier, model compatibility) and deterministic routing (self-serve backlog | product grooming | sales-assisted PS).
- Ensure observable signals (intake source, expected QPS, streaming or tool chains, structured schema complexity) are captured for prioritization and capacity planning.

Proposed decision rules (high level):
1) Eligibility gate: request must include minimal required artifacts: sample prompts, expected concurrency, success criteria (latency and accuracy thresholds), and a non-functional constraints list (PII, retention, region). Missing artifacts -> return to customer with intake checklist.
2) SLA mapping: map requested SLOs to intake buckets: Self-Serve (best-effort), Standard SLA (hosted-api baseline), Enterprise SLA (requires sales/commit or Dedicated). Any requested latency <150ms at 99th percentile or retention >90 days automatically escalates.
3) Routing by request type:
   - Single-turn chat + structured output -> product grooming track (evaluate SDK/contract changes)
   - Streaming with tool chains -> product + eng (runtime compatibility check)
   - Multi-tenant tool/function-calling with data residency -> sales/solutions + security + platform track
4) Tie-breakers: when capacity or priority conflict exists, prioritize requests with: high revenue potential, regulatory/regional risk, or platform security blockers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Triage checklist published in Confluence with form template and intake webhook for incoming requests.
- Playbook implemented as a decision flow in the intake workspace so reviewers can click through and get a deterministic routing outcome.
- Two-week pilot with top 10 inbound enterprise requests proving decision time <=48 hours and correct routing in >=80% of cases.

Operational notes: capture the intake metadata in our intake dashboard (fields: customer_id, tenant_size, requested_qps, streaming: yes/no, tool_chain_complexity, structured_schema_sample_size, required_SLOs). This data feeds the capacity & cost forecast runbook and will be used by Sales to propose contract changes.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Risk: over-automation may route nuanced requests incorrectly; mitigation: human review fallback and weekly calibration meetings.
- Trade-off: strict eligibility reduces noise but may frustrate PMs/AE; mitigation: fast human feedback loop with sample asks and templates.

Deliverables:
- Confluence playbook + intake form (owner: PM).
- Triage routing rules implemented in intake pipeline (owner: Eng).
- Intake dashboard widgets (owner: Product Analytics).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Published playbook and intake form linked from the Hosted API docs. 2) Routing engine returns deterministic route for 95% of sample requests in pilot set. 3) Pilot shows avg decision time <=48 hours and stakeholder satisfaction >=80% in feedback. 4) Dashboard shows captured intake fields for first 30 pilot requests.
